essence: Secondaries measured against chiefs — king's man, brahmin's; other chiefs, other unities — king's horse, man (vv19-20).
Course told, delusion denied, seal spoken: Māyā-knower-resting intellects drive transaction, moment-grounded in self-awareness; told, proved, unrefuted, useful, full apparatus besides (vv21-23).

sections.SUMMARY: One short of the pure chief, secondaries mutually fit — the king's man, and the brahmin's. By other chiefs, other unities — relation-called of secondaries: the king's horse, man. Thus relation's course is told: intellects resting on Māyā-knowers, of varied views, driving transaction. Not deluded, though called so — all, moment by moment, grounded in endless-awareness reflection called self-awareness. Told, self-awareness-proved, unrefuted, useful — relation in recognition: full apparatus besides.
sections.FUNCTION: Closes by measure and verdict: pairs, course, denial, seal.
sections.KEY TERMS: ekahāni (one-short) · guṇa/pradhāna (secondary/chief) · saṃbandhākhyā (relation-called) · saṃbandhagati (course) · svasaṃvit (self-awareness) · parikara (apparatus)
sections.LOCAL CONTEXT: Passage 3 of 3: vv. 19–23. Close of the third proof; colophon paratext.
sections.EXPLANATION: Pairs measured; course told; delusion denied by moment-grounding; seal in four predicates plus full apparatus.
sections.BOUNDARY: ekahānyā held open. No live forks.
sections.RELATED: Sāṅkhya pair · Nyāya parts · Ajad v25 seal · Pratyabhijñā · Vyas 1989

rasa.sthayibhava: utsāha (exultation) as measure, course, denial, seal land in turn
rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is exultation: the proof closes the way treatises close — measured, told, defended, sealed. The vyabhicāri is relief that delusion is denied without new machinery. Seal relished.
